inFlight.what: The loop's sprite priority swap - designed, never built, and it is why loops look flat

blockedOnOwner.what: How far to go on getting video memory back for objects. Three levers, measured, and they add up rather than compete. My recommendation gets you about 384 tiles back - objects from 152 to roughly 536 - and the work that unlocks it is the same background streamer the region plan already needs. The option I recommend AGAINST would get you 512 but quietly kills two effects items you asked for.

The last 184 pixels of the red spring still shift colour under Knuckles - the coil's mid-tone. Every palette slot is spoken for on both sides so it cannot be relabelled away. Cheap option: the spring drops its fifth grey onto a neighbouring shade (that slot is one Sonic uses for three pixels in his whole sheet). The alternative changes Knuckles himself across about 646 of his 4092 tiles, which I would avoid.

nextBoundary: When the priority swap lands, or blocks on a look call that is yours.
